title: How to use cursor on mac to ipad in Finder on a Mac easily
metaTitle: How to use cursor on Mac to iPad with Universal Control
description: Learn how to use cursor on Mac to iPad using Universal Control. Follow our step by step guide to control your iPad with your Mac mouse and keyboard today.
targetKeyword: use cursor on mac to ipad
intro: You can use your Mac cursor on an iPad by enabling a feature called Universal Control. This allows your mouse and keyboard to cross the screen boundary and interact with your iPad as if it were an external display.
tldr: Ensure both devices use the same Apple Account.
Turn on Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and Handoff on both devices.
Enable Cursor and Keyboard in your Mac and iPad settings.
Place devices near each other and push the cursor toward the iPad edge.

stats.label: Maximum devices connected to Mac at once

blocks.text: Universal Control is the system feature that lets you use your Mac cursor on an iPad. It is not an app you open in Finder. Instead, it is a background process that bridges your input devices. Once set up, you simply move your mouse pointer past the edge of your Mac screen. The iPad detects the cursor and allows you to click, scroll, and type using your Mac hardware.

Before you start, check your software versions. You need at least macOS Monterey 12.3 and iPadOS 15.4. Both devices must be signed into the same Apple Account. Two-factor authentication must be active on your account. Keep devices within 10 meters of each other for a stable connection.

items: Wi-Fi must be enabled on both devices.
Handoff must be active on both.
Neither device can share an internet connection.

blocks.text: Step by Step Setup on Mac
You must enable the feature in your System Settings. This tells your Mac to look for nearby iPads to share your input devices.

items: Open the Apple menu and select System Settings.
Click the Advanced button if you see it.
Turn on the switch for Allow your pointer and keyboard to move between any nearby Mac or iPad.

blocks.text: Configuring your iPad for Cursor Input
Your iPad also needs permission to accept input from your Mac. Without this, the Mac cursor will not cross over to the iPad screen.

items: Toggle the Cursor and Keyboard switch to on.

blocks.text: How to Use the Cursor on iPad

Once configured, place your iPad next to your Mac. Move your cursor toward the edge of the Mac screen that faces the iPad. You will see a small border appear on the iPad edge. Keep pushing the cursor through that border to move it onto the iPad display.
If the cursor moves to the wrong side, go to System Settings > Displays > Arrange. Drag the iPad icon to match where it sits on your desk.
blocks.title: Arrange Displays

faq.question: Can I use Universal Control with any iPad?
faq.answer: You need an iPad running iPadOS 15.4 or later. Most iPads released in the last few years support this feature.

faq.question: Does it work if I use a VPN?
faq.answer: No. VPNs often block the local network discovery required for Universal Control to find your iPad.

task: How to use cursor on mac to ipad
requirements: Same Apple Account on both devices

steps.name: Enable on Mac
steps.text: Go to System Settings, click Displays, then enable the pointer and keyboard setting.

steps.name: Enable on iPad
steps.text: Go to Settings, then General, then AirPlay and Continuity, and toggle Cursor and Keyboard.

troubleshooting.problem: Cursor does not cross to iPad
troubleshooting.fix: Toggle Handoff off and on again on both devices.
Restart both your Mac and your iPad to clear connection states.

lazur.spoken: Where is the setting to allow my Mac cursor on the iPad?
lazur.result: Lazur points to the 'Allow your pointer and keyboard' toggle in Displays settings.
